narrative.title: Bundling Grant Line Items, Once Each
narrative.scenario: A finance clerk bundles expense line items toward an exact grant total, but each line item on the sheet may be used at most once — even when two items carry the same amount, they are separate lines. After sorting the sheet, the clerk builds bundles by taking an item and moving on, or skipping ahead; when several identical amounts sit side by side, only the first may open a branch at that depth, so no bundle is ever filed twice.
narrative.inputFormat: An array candidates of positive integers (duplicates allowed) and an integer target.
narrative.outputFormat: Every unique combination summing to target, sorted lexicographically by the verifier.

complexity.optimalTime: O(2^n) branch walks in the worst case
complexity.optimalSpace: O(target) recursion depth beyond the output

testCases.explanation: Four unique bundles; the two 1s are distinct items, which is why [1, 1, 6] exists but no bundle appears twice.
The 5 alone works, and one pair of 2s joins the single 1; duplicate 2-branches collapse.

hintLevels: Level 1: Two rules separate this from unlimited reuse: a taken item advances the index, and equal neighbours may not both open branches.
Level 2: Sort first. On the take branch recurse with index + 1 and the reduced target; on the skip branch, step the index past every twin of the current value.
Level 3: The twin-skip loop runs after backtracking, before the exclusion call — that placement is what makes the dedup work at every depth, not just the top.
